gen-eater-gf-open-sans: Eater's thin strokes never shrink to hairlines, sitting just beside slightly heavier stems with wide gaps between letters. And Open Sans below it is smooth and modern, its bulky lowercase keeping every curve open and unclogged.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-ogham: The body text reads clean and contemporary, its lowercase looking bold because the letter bodies are so large. Noto Sans Ogham supplies the openness, wide gaps in the e echoing Almendra Display's ornate letters that never pinch shut.
gen-audiowide-gf-prompt: Audiowide sets its letters like spaced tiles, all marker-plain strokes. It carries the futuristic punch, while Prompt handles the everyday reading with oversized small letters and open apertures that keep each word clear.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-old-hu: The body text reads approachable, with large counters in a, e and s that stay open at tiny sizes. Noto Sans Old Hungarian would carry page after page without strain, while Almendra Display adds the ornate, literary flourish.
gen-audiowide-gf-radio-canada: Audiowide draws its letters with no swell or thinning, each glyph spaced like a tile between wide grout lines. Radio Canada brings full c, s and z shapes and a clear opening at the end of every curve.
gen-eater-gf-questrial: Questrial cuts every stroke flat at a single weight, with open round letters and short stalks above. And Eater, with its subtle weight shifts like etched lines in glass, supplies the dark bite against that flatness.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-radio-canada-big: Round and loud: Autour One keeps its strokes uniform and barely steps down from capitals to lowercase. But Radio Canada Big does the quiet work, its monoline sans-serif letters filling the line with terminals finishing well away from the stem.
gen-eater-gf-readex-pro: Eater snarls with soft-contrast curves and wide gaps between letters. Readex Pro takes over for reading, its crossbars matching the stems and its weight holding steady from word to word, so lengthy paragraphs would glide by.
gen-flavors-gf-roboto: Flavors towers with a stubby carpenter's-pencil x-height, its bowls and diagonals drawn as sturdy as the stems. And Roboto, clean and contemporary with generous mouths on its round letters, would keep pages of text moving smoothly.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-ruda: Autour One rounds out its expressive, bold letters with no hairline-to-stem shift and barely any step from capitals to lowercase. Ruda's wire-like monoline lowercase keeps long reading smooth on screen.
